name: Coral bleaching
summary: No new global bleaching event declared as of 14 Nov; scientists warn El Niño heat could bring one this year
state: Searches on 14 Nov found no declaration of a fifth global bleaching event and no confirmed regional mass bleaching. A global reef status report published on 31 Aug found gaps between bleaching events now average five to six years and said record ocean temperatures and El Niño could bring another event this year (bdnews24). NOAA's August outlook gave a greater than 70% chance of Alert Level 1 heat stress across most of the Caribbean by early November (GCRMN, 14 Aug), so the level stays Normal with an upward trend.
for_you: Most exposed are coastal communities that rely on reef fisheries, tourism and storm protection, especially in the Caribbean and Pacific. Divers and visitors may see bleached reefs where heat stress builds.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event in progress or regional mass bleaching confirmed: Normal line

sources.title: bdnews24 — Coral bleaching occurring too frequently for reefs to recover, scientists say

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.
